name: Tamoxifen
route_note: oral tablets or solution once daily, typically for 5–10 years in adjuvant therapy

discovery.by: Dora Richardson and Arthur Walpole's team, ICI Pharmaceuticals
discovery.note: Synthesised in a contraceptive programme; it proved a poor contraceptive but an effective anti-oestrogen in breast cancer, championed clinically by V. Craig Jordan.

tagline: First targeted cancer therapy: an oestrogen-receptor modulator for breast cancer
summary: Tamoxifen is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator that blocks oestrogen action in breast tissue while acting as a partial agonist in bone and the uterus. It reduces recurrence and death in oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer, is used for risk reduction in high-risk women, and is on the WHO essential medicines list.
mechanism: Tamoxifen and its more potent metabolites 4-hydroxytamoxifen and endoxifen bind the oestrogen receptor and induce a conformation that recruits co-repressors instead of co-activators in breast tissue, blocking oestrogen-driven proliferation.

In endometrium, bone and liver the same complex acts as a partial agonist, explaining preserved bone density in postmenopausal women but increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia, cancer and thromboembolism.
Conversion to endoxifen depends on CYP2D6, so strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may reduce efficacy.
uses: Adjuvant treatment of ER-positive early breast cancer (pre- and postmenopausal)
Ductal carcinoma in situ after surgery and radiotherapy
Reduction of breast cancer risk in high-risk women
Male breast cancer; off-label: gynaecomastia, ovulation induction

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: ICI chemist Dora Richardson synthesises ICI 46,474.

history.title: First clinical study
history.detail: Cole and colleagues at the Christie Hospital report responses in advanced breast cancer.

history.title: UK approval
history.detail: Licensed in the UK as Nolvadex for advanced breast cancer.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US for metastatic breast cancer.

history.title: EBCTCG overview
history.detail: The first Early Breast Cancer Trialists' overview confirms that adjuvant tamoxifen reduces recurrence and death.

history.title: Risk reduction
history.detail: NSABP P-1 shows a 49% reduction in invasive breast cancer in high-risk women; FDA approves risk-reduction use.

history.title: ATLAS
history.detail: Ten years of tamoxifen reduces recurrence and mortality compared with five years.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4/5 and CYP2D6 to endoxifen and 4-hydroxytamoxifen

safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning (risk reduction and DCIS settings): uterine malignancies, stroke and pulmonary embolism.

facts: Tamoxifen is often called the first targeted cancer therapy because it acts on a defined molecular target, the oestrogen receptor.
